note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Jun 22 - Jul 24, 2026). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: Burlington landed at number six on a national top-towns-to-visit list. What would you show a skeptic first?
There's an official Vermont creemee passport now. Which stand gets your first stamp?
Front Porch Forum just turned twenty. What's the wildest thing you've seen on there?
Beta keeps getting bigger — new campus space, new jobs. If electric flights start leaving Burlington someday, where should the first one go?
Italian American families have been farming Colchester for a hundred years. Which local farm or family business do you hope is still around in another hundred?
A land trust just bought two thousand acres in the Champlain Valley to keep it wild forever. Where's your favorite piece of untouched Vermont?
Leunig's is opening a spot in South Burlington's City Center. Good move or is it a Church Street thing?
Kountry Kart is doing late-night again. What's your order?
Vermont game stores are turning into little clubhouses — chess nights, card leagues. What game could get you out on a weeknight?
The Champlain Parkway finally opened. It took sixty-one years. Have you driven it yet?
Noah Kahan fans keep stealing the same Vermont road sign. What's the farthest you've ever gone for a musician you love?
Vermont's rethinking air conditioning as summers heat up. What's your move when the house won't cool down?
Seven Days spent twenty-four straight hours on Church Street. What do you think 3 AM looks like out there?
A Vermont filmmaker is documenting all one hundred of Vermont's covered bridges. How many do you think you've crossed?
Lippa's Jewelry left Church Street after ninety-three years. What shop would you miss most?
The Vermont Green women finished their first season as national runners-up — and never lost a match all year. Has Burlington ever had a team like this?
A Malletts Bay couple has found five thousand objects on the bottom of Lake Champlain — including an 1819 steamboat. What do you figure is still down there?
The old Courtyard Marriott downtown just became The Harborvale after a nineteen-million-dollar makeover. What Burlington place do you still call by its old name?
Festival of Fools takes over Church Street next weekend — eighteen years running. What's the best street act you've ever stopped for?
Vermont's first soccer bar just opened in Shelburne — ten TVs and an owner from North London. Which sport is better in a room full of strangers?
The Essex doughnut baker who outgrew her home kitchen in eighteen months is moving into Leo & Co. What's your doughnut order?
Shelburne Museum is putting up its fortieth building — a Native American art center a decade in the making. When were you last out on that campus?
Vermont spent fourteen years as its own republic — its own money, its own post office. What Vermont fact belongs in every visitor's first-day briefing?
The Vermont Renaissance Faire runs seventy vendors deep, half in handmade costume. What costume could talk you into going all in?
Two new novels just turned real Vermont villages into fiction. Which local town would you cast in a mystery?
